newsitem.title: UK: Smiths results lift shares, prompt upgrades.
newsitem.headline: Smiths results lift shares, prompt upgrades.

text.p: Shares in Smiths Industries shrugged off a weaker UK stock market as results at the top end of expectations prompted analysts to raise forecasts for the diversified industrial group.
Pre-tax profits of 165 million stg and a dividend of 16.2p per share for the year both topped most estimates in the market and by mid-afternoon Smiths' shares were trading 10p higher at 801-1/2p.
Good cash generation continued to underpin the company's performance and provide fuel to maintain earnings momentum, said analysts.
"That remains the key for the continued outperformance," said Panmure Gordon analyst Paul Pickford.

"It gives them so much firepower to do earnings enhancing deals - and self-finance them. They've spent 475 million pounds (stg) since 1991 without recourse to shareholders and that's not going to stop."
Operating cashflow in the year to August rose to 149 million stg in 1996 from 140 million a year earlier.
The prospects for the group's aerospace division and growth opportunities in medical systems remained good said Pickford, who raised 1997 forecasts to 190 million stg from 187 million.

"The impetus in terms of aerospace is very much year two loaded, given the McDonnell Douglas strike slightly impacting 1997 numbers and the uplift in Boeing's production schedules being 1997 biased," said Pickford.
Another analyst, who preferred not to be named, said he was raising forecasts to around 183 million stg from 179 million stg.
